rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Meta just agreed to pay about $18 billion to settle lawsuits over how it handled children's data — a legal battle that had been building for roughly ten years. To put that in perspective, $18 billion is about what Meta earns in operating profit in a single quarter, so it's a big
risks: The settlement's carve-outs may be challenged or narrowly interpreted by regulators in future proceedings, limiting the legal 'safe harbor' benefit that appears to be priced into this resolution.

The $18B precedent may embolden plaintiffs or state attorneys general to pursue similarly scaled actions on adjacent privacy claims (adult data, cross-app tracking), increasing the frequency of large settlements going forward.
Cash outflow of ~$18B, while manageable, modestly reduces the capital available for AI infrastructure investment or buybacks in the near term.

A settlement may include binding product design mandates — algorithmic restrictions, time-limit defaults, or content ranking rules for minors — that partially constrain Meta's highest-engagement mechanics for a demographically critical cohort.

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: A financial news site published an article saying Deckers' stock is falling because of margin pressure, but the article itself isn't included — just the headline. Looking at the actual numbers Deckers has reported, gross margins are still above 57%, the company generates nearly $
risks: If margin pressure is confirmed as structural in the next earnings print — driven by discounting rather than deliberate marketing investment — it would elevate the risk of a brand-moat erosion narrative taking hold in the market, compressing the multiple further even if FCF holds.

SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM has built a new computer chip for its mainframe systems—the large, expensive computers that banks, governments, and big corporations use for their most critical operations—that can now also run AI applications directly. This matters because one of the biggest worries about IB
risks: If IBM monetizes AI-on-mainframe primarily through hardware upgrades rather than software licensing, margin accretion would be muted and the quality of incremental revenue would be lower than the thesis assumes.
Competitive response risk: AMD, Intel, and hyperscaler custom silicon teams may accelerate their own enterprise AI chip roadmaps, narrowing IBM's differentiation window.
Customer adoption risk: Mainframe customers tend to upgrade hardware on long cycles (5-7 years); near-term revenue impact may be minimal even if the technology is well-received.

Market sentiment divergence from management guidance creates the risk that when/if any guidance softening occurs, it will be disproportionately punished given elevated investor skepticism already priced into the stock.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: Google's cloud computing business has now grown to represent about one-fifth of the company's total revenue, which is a big deal because cloud contracts are more stable and recurring than advertising dollars. Alphabet also brought back a well-known AI expert, signaling it is figh
risks: Deepening the Marvell partnership concentrates a portion of AI infrastructure supply chain in a single custom silicon vendor, creating potential execution or delivery risk if Marvell faces capacity or design issues.
Rehiring an AI founder may signal that Alphabet has recently lost key AI talent or faces internal cultural friction in its AI divisions, which would be a lagging negative signal worth monitoring.

A $12.2B capital commitment to a single silicon partner concentrates supply-chain risk — if Marvell underdelivers on chip performance or roadmap, Google has limited near-term alternatives at this scale.
Custom silicon partnerships require deep engineering coordination; talent or integration failures could delay cost benefits and create stranded capital.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: NVIDIA just agreed to pay $6 billion to license AI software from a startup called Poolside that specializes in AI that writes code. Think of it like a restaurant paying a premium for a signature sauce recipe to add to its menu — it doesn't mean the kitchen can't cook, it means th
risks: If NVIDIA pursues a pattern of large external model licenses, cumulative licensing costs could meaningfully burden FCF and signal a strategic dependency on third-party AI capabilities.
Licensing Poolside's code-generation model creates a latent conflict-of-interest risk if Poolside later competes for enterprise software contracts that NVIDIA also pursues.

If the OpenAI guarantee reduction reflects a broader pattern of hyperscaler and large-customer capex renegotiations rather than a one-off project timing adjustment, near-term revenue visibility could deteriorate — we would need to see corroborating signals from other customers or from NVIDIA's own backlog disclosures.

Concentration risk is highlighted: a single customer commitment at this scale being renegotiated is a reminder that NVIDIA's near-term revenue profile has meaningful dependence on a small number of very large buyers.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: Two news stories came out suggesting that large companies are moving from testing Microsoft's AI tools to actually using them at scale in their businesses — which is the main thing the investment case is betting on. Separately, Nvidia said something that implies Microsoft has a h
risks: Industry narrative of 'pilot to production' may be running ahead of actual contract-level revenue, creating expectation risk if Microsoft's next earnings report shows slower Copilot seat growth than the narrative implies.

The $678B backlog figure attributed to Nvidia commentary is unverified and may represent total addressable opportunity rather than committed revenue, risking disappointment if used as a valuation anchor.
Epistemic risk: the AI monetization thesis cannot be independently verified from public disclosures, meaning investors must rely entirely on management's qualitative framing.

Regulatory and investor backlash risk: the SEC or large institutional investors may eventually pressure Microsoft to provide more granular AI disclosure, potentially revealing a monetization gap relative to market expectations.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: Amazon's CEO said he thinks AWS — their cloud business — could one day reach $1 trillion in revenue. The math checks out if AWS keeps growing at roughly its current pace for another 13-15 years. But this is a long-range aspiration, not a new forecast or product announcement. Noth
risks: If Anthropic's valuation collapses pre- or post-IPO, Amazon bears reputational risk around its AI capital allocation narrative, even if the dollar loss (~$8B committed) is manageable relative to Amazon's balance sheet.

Anthropic pursuing an IPO at a high valuation could accelerate competition: a well-capitalized public Anthropic may pursue its own cloud or inference infrastructure, reducing dependency on AWS over time.

If the $25B AI run rate figure is compositionally dominated by low-margin infrastructure (raw compute rental) rather than high-margin software services, the margin uplift thesis could be weaker than assumed.

Competitors (Microsoft, Google) are reporting comparable AI momentum, meaning the $25B figure may reflect industry-wide demand rather than Amazon-specific share gains — making it a rising-tide story rather than a moat-widening one.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify's stock jumped about 5% today, but there was no news behind it — no earnings, no product announcement, no guidance change. That kind of move on no information is just market noise. The business itself — its millions of merchants, its payments and financial tools, its grow
risks: AI commerce strategy adds execution risk: if Shopify is investing heavily in AI tooling to stay ahead, this may pressure near-term margins or require capital allocation that delays FCF margin expansion.

AI-native commerce platforms (e.g., those building directly on LLM infrastructure) could bypass traditional storefront software entirely — the Q2 call highlights this is on management's radar, suggesting competitive intensity is real.
Valuation-to-fair-value gap (current price ~16x base case fair value) means any miss or guidance cut would cause severe price dislocations, even if the long-term thesis remains intact.
A 17% single-day move compresses the margin of safety further on an already premium valuation, making the stock more sensitive to any future guidance miss.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir's AI software business with the Pentagon is reportedly closing in on $1 billion a year in revenue. This matters because it shows the U.S. military is deeply relying on Palantir's tools for real decisions — not just piloting them — which is exactly what the investment the
risks: Customer concentration risk increases if Pentagon AI approaches or exceeds ~15-20% of total revenue, making any DoD budget cut or political disruption more materially impactful.
A single large relationship invites scrutiny: if this revenue is tied to a small number of specific programs, contract non-renewal risk is elevated relative to a diversified customer base.

Program of Record status increases Palantir's formal visibility within DoD procurement, which could attract incumbent defense contractors (Lockheed, Raytheon, Palantir-adjacent primes) to compete more aggressively at re-compete cycles.

Formal acquisition status subjects Maven to additional government oversight, audit requirements, and potential congressional scrutiny that may increase compliance costs or introduce operational constraints.

rows.name: Lululemon Athletica Inc.
rows.last_memo: Lululemon is showing weakness in its two most important growth areas at the same time: its home US market and China, which was supposed to be its big international opportunity. An analyst at UBS is warning that the company may soon officially lower its profit expectations for the
risks: Simultaneous US and China softness raises the risk that the growth deceleration is brand-structural, not macro-cyclical, making recovery timing unpredictable.
A formal guidance cut could trigger institutional selling given the stock's prior premium growth multiple, potentially creating a self-reinforcing de-rating.

If management responds to weak US comps with increased promotions, it risks permanently repricing consumer expectations for the brand — the most damaging long-term outcome for a premium positioning thesis.
China softness may reflect local competitive dynamics (domestic athletic brands like Anta and Li-Ning gaining share) that are harder to reverse than macro slowdowns.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: The IRS is apparently looking into UnitedHealth's taxes, but we don't know why, how much money is at stake, or when it will be resolved. On its own, this is not a reason to change the investment view — UnitedHealth makes about $24 billion in cash per year and carries relatively m
risks: IRS scrutiny could result in material back-tax liability, penalties, or required restatements if the subject matter involves aggressive tax positions — scope and dollar exposure are currently unknown.

If scrutiny relates to intercompany transfer pricing between UnitedHealthcare and Optum, it could draw regulatory attention to the integrated model's economics, though this is speculative without further detail.
IRS determination that foreign subsidiary tax structures were improper could result in back taxes, interest, and penalties that reduce cumulative FCF by an unknown but potentially material amount.

If IRS probe results in earnings restatements, the quality of historically reported profits would be called into question, damaging investor confidence and potentially triggering debt covenant reviews.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: AST SpaceMobile's stock has dropped nearly half its value in three months, which is a serious warning sign even if we don't yet know exactly why. The company is burning through about $1.8 billion in cash per year and has not yet built meaningful revenue — it's essentially a techn
risks: A 47.5% equity price decline materially increases the cost of equity capital, making future dilutive raises more expensive and more damaging to existing shareholders if the company must raise near current prices.
If the decline reflects leaked or anticipated negative milestone news not yet publicly confirmed, there is an information asymmetry risk that should be resolved before adding to the position.
Sustained negative price momentum in a pre-profitability name can create a self-reinforcing dynamic: weaker stock price → more dilutive financing needed → further pressure on per-share value.

SpaceX, with superior regulatory leverage and deployed satellite infrastructure, could secure priority rights to the contested spectrum band, permanently impairing ASTS's service capacity or geographic reach.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Tesla announced it will hold a special event about its Semi truck on September 24, and separately confirmed it is taking its robotaxi service beyond the initial test cities of Austin and Miami. These are both genuine positive steps — the robotaxi program is alive and growing rath
risks: Semi event on Sept. 24 creates a concrete management credibility checkpoint — a vague or marketing-heavy presentation without production ramp data would be a mild negative signal on capital allocation discipline.

Robotaxi expansion into new cities before unit economics in Austin/Miami are publicly validated raises the risk that Tesla is scaling a business whose profitability is unproven, potentially increasing regulatory scrutiny and capital consumption.

Expansion of autonomous vehicle operations across more jurisdictions multiplies regulatory risk surface area — a single high-profile incident in a new market could trigger multi-state regulatory pauses.

Solar Roof exit signals possible broader difficulty in scaling consumer energy products, raising questions about whether the residential energy platform is viable without solar generation as an anchor.
